questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He asked me if I knew where his keys were.
options_en: He said, "Where did I put my keys?"
He said to me, "Do you know where my keys are?"
He said, "Do you know where my keys were?"
He asked, "Can you find my keys?"
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", and "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech are changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the past indefinite. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the present indefinite.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

"asked me" changes to "said to me".

"if" changes to "do".

"knew" changes to "know".

"were" changes to "are".

"I" changes to "you".

"His" changes to "my".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "He said to me, "Do you know where my keys are?""

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

These burrows need / to be wide dug / for the free / flow of water.
questions.solution_en:
In the part mentioned in option (a), the verb 'dug' is incorrectly qualified by the adjective 'wide' instead of an adverb. The adverb 'widely' is to be used in the place of the adjective 'wide'.

The correct sentence is: These burrows need to be widely dug for the free flow of water.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

Qualifiers: A word or phrase that limits the meaning of another word or phrase or makes it less general. 'Adverbs' and 'adjectives' are qualifiers.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The secretary to my boss is very efficient as he not only gives him the required information and also handles correspondence independently.
questions.solution_en: The most suitable option to substitute the underlined segment in the sentence is 'but also handles'. In the given sentence, the phrase 'not only' is used to introduce the first of two or more alternatives that are being considered for concurrency, while 'but also' is used to introduce the second of two or more items that are to be connected. The use of 'but also' in the sentence helps to maintain the intended parallelism of the two actions performed by the secretary, simultaneously. It effectively demonstrates that the secretary not only provides the required information but also independently manages correspondence. The other options either do not provide the necessary concurrency or do not fit grammatically within the structure of the sentence. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We can't underestimate the importance of teamwork, _______?
questions.solution_en:
The correct option to fill in the blank is 'can we'. In question tags, when the main clause is negative, the question tag should be positive, and vice versa. In the given sentence, the main clause is negative, indicating that the question tag should be positive. Also, if there is a modal verb (could, can, should, etc.) in the main sentence/clause, the question tag is also constructed with the same modal verb. In the given sentence, the modal verb 'can' is used. Accordingly, option (b) is correct as it uses the correct modal verb 'can' and also maintains the opposite polarity (negative main sentence, positive question tag).

Option (a) is not correct as it uses the wrong modal verb 'should' instead of 'can'.

Options (c) and (d) are not correct because they do not adhere to the grammatical rule that a negative main clause should have a positive question tag.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

Modal verb: A verb used with another verb to express an idea such as possibility that is not expressed by the main verb. The modal verbs in English are "can," "could," "may," "might," "must," "ought," "shall," "should," "will," and "would." They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. Here 'can' expresses the ability of the person to speak (main verb) Spanish. This ability cannot be expressed by the main verb 'speak'.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Biomimicry, the practice of drawing inspiration from nature to solve human challenges, is revolutionizing modern engineering. Nature, through millions of years of evolution, has perfected designs that are energy-efficient, sustainable, and highly adaptable. Engineers are increasingly looking to the natural world to develop innovative solutions to complex problems, whether in architecture, manufacturing, or materials science.

One of the most famous examples of biomimicry is the development of Velcro. The idea came from Swiss engineer George de Mestral, who observed how burrs stuck to his dog's fur. By mimicking the hook-and-loop mechanism of the burrs, Mestral created a fastening system that is now widely used. Another key example is the design of energy-efficient buildings inspired by termite mounds. Termites construct their nests with natural ventilation systems that maintain a stable temperature, even in extreme heat. Inspired by this, architects have designed climate-responsive buildings that reduce the need for artificial heating or cooling, saving energy.

In materials science, the lotus leaf's ability to resist dirt and water has led to the development of self-cleaning surfaces. These surfaces use microstructures similar to those on the leaf, preventing the accumulation of dust or grime. Similarly, researchers are studying the structure of spider silk, which is both incredibly strong and lightweight, to create synthetic materials for use in everything from medical sutures to aerospace components.

Biomimicry offers more than just clever designs. It emphasizes the importance of sustainability. By mimicking nature's solutions, engineers can create technologies that work in harmony with the environment, reducing waste and conserving resources. As this field continues to grow, it promises a future where human innovation is increasingly aligned with the natural world.

What is the central idea expressed about biomimicry?
options_en: It is a method of copying nature purely for aesthetic purposes in design.
It is a traditional practice used mainly in agricultural systems.
It is transforming engineering by using nature-inspired solutions that are efficient and adaptable.
It discourages innovation by relying entirely on natural forms.
questions.solution_en:
The passage describes biomimicry as a modern and growing field that draws inspiration from nature's designs, refined over millions of years, to solve human challenges. These solutions are noted for being energy-efficient, sustainable, and highly adaptable, and they are influencing areas like architecture, manufacturing, and materials science.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Option (a) is incorrect because the focus is on function and efficiency, not just aesthetics.

Option (b) is incorrect since the passage discusses engineering, not agriculture.

Option (d) misrepresents biomimicry, which encourages innovation through nature-inspired ideas rather than discouraging it.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This internal clock plays a critical role in regulating various physiological processes, including sleep-wake cycles, hormone release, eating habits, and body temperature.

B. It is primarily influenced by external cues, especially daylight, which helps synchronize our biological rhythms with the Earth's 24-hour cycle of day and night.

C. Consequently, disrupting this natural rhythm through irregular schedules or exposure to artificial light at night can lead to various long-term health issues.

D. The circadian rhythm is essentially a natural, internal process that functions as a master clock within the human body, guiding its daily operations.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is DBAC. Sentence D provides a clear and concise definition of the "circadian rhythm," making it the natural starting point for the paragraph. Sentence B logically follows by explaining how "It" (the circadian rhythm) is controlled or "influenced by external cues" like daylight. Sentence A then expands on the function of "This internal clock," listing the specific physiological processes it regulates. Finally, sentence C concludes the paragraph by explaining the negative consequences of "disrupting this natural rhythm," which follows logically after the description of its normal function. This creates a coherent flow from definition to control mechanism, function, and finally the consequences of disruption.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The blind man said to me, "Can you help me cross the road?"
options_en: The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.
The blind man asked me if I will help him cross the road.
The blind man asked me if I could help him crossed the road.
The blind man asked me if I can help him cross the road.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, when converting direct speech into indirect speech, the present modal verbs (can/may/must/will/shall) should be changed into past modal verbs (could/might/had to/would/should).

Example: She said, "I can speak ten languages." (Direct Speech)

She said that she could speak ten languages. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to me' is changed to 'asked me'.

'If' is introduced in the sentence.

'Can you' will be changed to 'I could'

'Help me' will be changed to 'Help him'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.

Also, when converting direct speech into indirect speech, the present modal verbs (can/may/must/will/shall) should be changed into past modal verbs (could/might/had to/would/should).

Example: She said, "I can speak ten languages." (Direct Speech)

She said that she could speak ten languages. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to me' is changed to 'asked me'.

'If' is introduced in the sentence.

'Can you' will be changed to 'I could'

'Help me' will be changed to 'Help him'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): The blind man asked me if I could help him cross the road.
